note: P4333 (Pro 28:23) — who rebukes a man will afterward find more favour than the flatterer.

dims.v: honest reproof — the rebuke that in the end wins more favour than flattery
the rebuking of a man that afterward wins more favour than flattery — the honest reproof that, though it stings at first, earns lasting gratitude, unlike the flatterer's momentary charm
the flattery it is set against (266650)
set against the flattering tongue that pleases then fails

yakach (rebuke/reprove) — 'whoever REBUKES a man will afterward find more favor than he who flatters'; honest correction, resented at first, is valued in the end above flattery. Emergent: the reprover ultimately more loved than the flatterer (cf 27:5-6; 29:5).
flattery — the smooth tongue that pleases now but fails in the end
the flattering with the tongue that pleases for the moment but wins less lasting favour than honest rebuke — smooth speech that gratifies now and is valued less in the end
the honest rebuke it is set against (266644)
set against the reprover who wins lasting favour

chalaq (be smooth/flatter) — 'than he who FLATTERS with his tongue'; flattery charms momentarily but earns less true favour than an honest rebuke. Emergent: the flatterer preferred at first, forgotten at last (cf 26:28; 29:5).
